newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Dow drives Australian stocks to record close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Dow drives Australian stocks to record close.

text.p: The Australian share market stormed to a record close on Wednesday after U.S. markets rallied on consumer price data that eased US inflation concerns.

The market set sail higher right from the opening bell and by midsession was cruising in uncharted waters, reaching a record intraday high of 2,444.2. This surpasssed the previous record high of 2,438.8, set on January 10, 1997.

By 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was up 18.8 points at 2,438.2, surpassing the previous record close of 2424.6, set on December 31. March share price index futures were up 14 points at 2,450, an 11.8 point premium to the index.
"A stronger Dow and a stronger bond market had us looking good for the day," said a Melbourne broker.

The gold sector was dragging the chain after the bullion price continued to slide offshore but gains were generally widely spread, with the resources sector boosted marginally more than the industrials grouping.

The world's largest zinc producer, Pasminco, impressed from the start as its shares soared over nine percent to A$2.24 on the back of a buoyant zinc price and investor approval of the benefits to be obtained from its proposed purchase of CRA's Century Zinc project in north Queensland.

Nickel miner QNI did not fare as well, its shares sliding over four percent early before recovering some ground to close just two cents lower at A$2.68 following a first half profit downgrade announced after the market closed on Tuesday.

At the smaller end, junior explorer Dragon Mining came out breathing fire in the afternoon, its shares leaping 48 percent to A$0.17 after it announced a nickel find at its 35 percent-owned Weld Range prospect in Western Australia.
Shares in Sons of Gwalia, which owns the other 65 percent of Weld Range, added only eight cents to close at A$6.75, but well off its early bullion-depressed lows of A$6.60.
The outlook was upbeat with the uptrend seen holding, even if profit takers cashed in some gains in the near term.
"There is still very good support for the likes of the banks. I think the tone looks pretty reasonable," the broker said.
Rises barely shaded falls, while about 31 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures business was moderate while options trade was very busy as players took trading opportunities on the back of the strong rise in underlying markets.
Total options traded 46,108 (24,843)
Turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 6,501 (2,363)

In other local markets, Australian bond's robust recovery from last Friday's U.S payrolls-inspired sell off ran into some technical resistance but traders said the tone was positive and the market was expected to remain well supported.
Bonds were boosted in offshore trade by a rally in Treasuries, following better than expected U.S. CPI data, and continued to push ahead from the open of floor trading.
By 5.15 p.m. (0615 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.44 percent, down from Tuesday's 7.53 percent.
The Australian dollar was back under pressure late Wednesday due to a sudden flare-up in long running concerns over the health of Japanese investor demand.

The currency had steadied at 78 cents in the morning as talk of a domestic rate cut went off the boil, but was then dumped to US$0.7770 support by offshore players. Traders said the latest scare sprang from a Japanese newspaper report that Japanese investors were shifting funds from A$ bonds to U.S. assets.
By 5.15 p.m. (0615 GMT) the local dollar had subsided to US$0.7776/81 from an early US$0.7803/08, to stand little changed from Tuesday's weak US$0.7778/84 finish.
